- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast bias by 5–10% relative to recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots downward — cap forecast decline to 1–2% below peak for next 5 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0–0.3), model frequently underestimates downward moves — add 2–5% buffer to forecast for next 7 days.
- Mean reversion is overestimated in early forecast horizon — for 30-day forecasts, apply 10–15% downward adjustment if recent 10-day average is > 10% above 30-day moving average.
- If sentiment turns sharply positive (e.g., > 0.5) after a downtrend, model often fails to capture rebound — increase forecast by 3–5% for next 5 days if sentiment > 0.4 and price > 65.
- Forecast lag is common in 30-day horizon — if true outcome is below 60, model often lags 1–2 days — adjust forecast to match true outcome 1–2 days ahead if sentiment is stable or mildly positive.
